title: John Keats: 231 Years Ago Today, the Poet With No Name on His Grave

lines: He died at twenty-five, with no name on his grave.
Who changed the world today? October 31.
Who changed the world today? October thirty-first.
231 years ago today, in London,
Two hundred thirty-one years ago today, in London,
the poet John Keats was born.
He lost his father at eight,
and later his mother to tuberculosis.
In 1815, he trained at Guy's Hospital.
In eighteen fifteen, he trained at Guy's Hospital.
A year later, he was licensed,
but told his guardian: I will be a poet.
In 1816, reading Homer in English
In eighteen sixteen, reading Homer in English
inspired a dazzling sonnet.
In 1818, his long poem Endymion
In eighteen eighteen, his long poem Endymion
was torn apart by the critics.
That winter, Tom, the brother he nursed,
died of it too.
In spring 1819, in Hampstead,
In spring eighteen nineteen, in Hampstead,
he fell for his neighbour, Fanny Brawne.
Within months, he wrote odes that would never die.
A friend said Ode to a Nightingale was written under a plum tree.
And Ode on a Grecian Urn ends with the words:
Beauty is truth, truth beauty.

scenes.chapter: Chapter 4  A name writ in water
lines: In February 1820, he coughed up blood and said:
In February eighteen twenty, he coughed up blood and said:
That drop of blood is my death warrant; I must die.
That September, he sailed for Rome with Joseph Severn.
He died in Rome on February 23, 1821, at twenty-five.
He died in Rome on February twenty-third, eighteen twenty-one, at twenty-five.
His gravestone bears no name, only:
Here lies one whose name was writ in water.
Ignored in his lifetime,
he is now one of the greatest English poets.
His question for you:
if no one understood your work, would you keep writing?

items.text: No one gets it. Keep writing?

lines: This is Who Changed the World Today,
and on October 31, we remember John Keats.
and on October thirty-first, we remember John Keats.
